LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. After a 4-1 start to the season, Baltimore has scored just 33 points in its last three games, losing to the Browns, Bengals, and Bills. On the other hand, Jacksonville is coming off a 42-7 win over the Colts and has won four of its last five games overall. The Jaguars are big road favorites with the total set at 40.5 on Thursday night. Let’s take a look at a few anytime touchdown scorer picks for Jaguars vs. Ravens on Thursday, Nov. 5. Jaguars vs. Ravens Best Touchdown Bets Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chris Rodriguez Jr. Anytime Touchdown (+100) Derrick Henry Anytime Touchdown (+120) Parker Washington Anytime Touchdown (+150) As Bhayshul Tuten deals with an injury, Chris Rodriguez Jr. could see more work out of Jacksonville’s backfield on a short week. He has been getting some solid usage as a backup anyway, totalling 33 snaps to Tuten’s 68 over the last two games. The former Washington Commander has also found the end zone a few times this season, including last week against the Colts. He ran for 41 yards and a score on just six carries against Indianapolis. I’ll take Rodriguez to score again this week in Baltimore. The Ravens are starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback, so Derrick Henry should see plenty of usage this week. The bruising back may be able to take advantage of the Jaguars defense on a short week after only carrying the ball 11 times last week in Buffalo. If the Ravens want a chance to win, they’re going to have to lean heavily on Henry. If they dig themselves into a whole, they won’t be able to use their running back nearly as much in the second half. For that reason, I also like Henry to score a first-quarter touchdown at a nice +650 price. He’s scored in the opening quarter in five of eight games this season, including last week. Taking him to score the first touchdown or the Ravens’ first touchdown could be worth a sprinkle as well. Parker Washington caught just one of two targets last week against Indianapolis, but I don’t see him being used that sparingly this week. Washington still leads the Jaguars with 48 targets this season, including 11 two games ago against Houston. The Jacksonville Jaguars are 8.5-point favorites as they visit the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. With the Ravens facing a full-blown quarterback disaster, my Jaguars vs. Ravens prediction and NFL picks are backing the visitors in what could be an absolute smackdown. TOP Pick Jaguars vs Ravens prediction: Jaguars -8.5 With rookie Joe Fagnano being the likely starter for the Baltimore Ravens , I'm expecting a bloodbath. Playable to -9.5. Fagnano completed just 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards against Buffalo and is now nursing an ankle injury on a short week. Baltimore hasn't topped 13 points in three straight games, sitting 30th in yards per play over that span . Meanwhile, the Jacksonville Jaguars ' offense is in a different galaxy right now, ranking third in yards per play over that stretch while scoring 73 points in its last two outings . The Ravens' defense has also been letting them down, allowing 71 points over its last two games. Isn't Jesse Minter supposed to be a defensive genius? Don't expect the Jaguars to play down to the competition. They're 12-3-1 ATS in their last 16 games as favorites, outscoring opponents by an average of 14 points and covering by an average of 8.6 points. Baltimore is 0-4-1 ATS in its last five games as a home underdog, losing by an average of 16 points. With the AFC's No. 1 seed to chase, Jacksonville has every reason to keep its foot on the gas. Jaguars vs Ravens combo Baltimore's quarterback situation might be the worst in the NFL. Playing on a short week against a Super Bowl contender makes matters even worse. Jacksonville has been an absolute bully against overmatched opponents , demolishing Indianapolis by 35 points as a 10.5-point favorite last week and smashing Cleveland by 24 as an 8.5-point favorite earlier this season. Let's pair another beatdown with a Brenton Strange touchdown. Baltimore has allowed a tight end to score in three of its last four games and has surrendered touchdowns on 83.3% of opponents' red-zone trips over its last three. This sets up beautifully for Strange to find the end zone in a Jacksonville rout. Brenton Strange anytime touchdown Jaguars vs Ravens touchdown scorer: Brenton Strange Baltimore's defense has been getting worked by tight ends, surrendering six touchdowns to the position this season . That's music to the ears of Strange, who's becoming a major piece of Jacksonville's passing attack. He's drawn at least seven targets in three of his last four games and enters Thursday as the Jaguars' second-most-targeted pass catcher this season. At just 28% on Kalshi, I'm buying the opportunity for Strange to find the end zone against this struggling defense. picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 10:16 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a strange injury-marred matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens . It's especially tough as the Ravens got hit at the QB position . But these teams meet in Week 9 on Thursday Night Football, and here are bold predictions. Life is better for the Jaguars. They're in the weaker AFC South division. They have a record of 5-2 and a three-game lead over the second-place Texans. Meanwhile, the Ravens are 4-4. That's worth last place in the tougher AFC North. It's a desperation game for the Ravens. Can they come up with a plan to move the football? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten will rush for 100-plus yards The Ravens have a fairly solid run defense. But there's a caveat to this prediction. The Jaguars won't need a lot of points to win this game. The Ravens will struggle to put points on the board as the Jaguars stack the box against Derrick Henry. That means the Jaguars will be content to pound the ground game once they get a double-digit lead. And that means more carries for Tuten. He's coming off a 104-yard rushing performance against the Colts. And he should hit the mark again. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he liked what he saw from Tuten, according to jacksonville.com. "I thought Tuten played really well (against the Colts)," Coen said. "He was seeing it. I thought he was a little more patient in this game. He was running through contact. He was explosive in the passing game. Tuten had a great week of practice, and it really carried over." Tuten said things fell into place , according to ESPN. "We knew it was going to rain," Tuten said. "We knew we were going to run the ball, and we just went out and imposed our will." Things are set up nicely for Tuten to have another big game. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence will throw three TD passes Even if Tuten runs up and down the field, the Ravens will commit to stopping him inside the 10-yard line. That will open up opportunities for Lawrence to complete drives with TD passes. This season, Lawrence has 17 touchdown passes with four interceptions. And Lawrence is trying to keep the Jaguars in all-business mode , according to news4jax.com. "Winning your division is really important, but I think for us, it's really just going week by week," Lawrence said. "It's not something we think, 'Oh, we're a few games up. We're in a good spot. We can relax.' That's not really at all how we think. We got a lot of football left." The Ravens have two choices on defense. They can take chances and try to create splash plays. Or they can sit back and try to keep the game close, where they could steal one in the fourth quarter. If they take chances against Lawrence, he will simply hit them with longer strikes. It seems like a no-win situation for the Ravens. And a big day for Lawrence and the Jaguars. Ravens RB Derrick Henry will set season high in carries Make no doubt about it. The Ravens are going to put a saddle on Henry and try to ride him to a victory. Henry has 24 carries twice this year. But his season high of 26 came against the Cowboys in overtime. Look for him to eclipse that number. That is, if the Ravens can keep the ball long enough for him to rack up carries while the game is still within reach. But it's possible the Ravens will feed Henry even if they fall behind by two scores. That's all because the only real path to a win is through Henry. Henry has been the recent subject of trade rumors because of the injury to Jackson. The Giants have been in that conversation, but head coach John Harbaugh said it's hard to make big trades , according to Giants.com. "We're going to do the most we can possibly do to try to get some things done," Harbaugh said. "It's hard to get deals done. It's hard. You can see how hard it is, but we're going to do our best and what's for our team. And the best thing we can do, the main thing we're going to do is focus on our guys and get ready to play the game. But all that other stuff is definitely going on behind the scenes at all times." For now, Henry remains with the Ravens. And he has to be their leader on Thursday night. TV: Prime Network (Al Michaels, Kirk Herbstreit, Kalee Hartung. Radio: 1010-XL/92.5-FM (Frank Frangie, Jeff Lageman, Bucky Brooks); Spanish: 106.7-FM (Javier Carrero, Victor Cora); SiriusXM Channel 814. Records: Jaguars 5-2, Ravens 4-4. ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks down at his thumb while walking off the field against the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) What happened last week? The Jaguars routed the Indianapolis Colts 42-7 at EverBank Stadium. The Ravens lost 36-10 at Buffalo. What are the Jaguars-Ravens odds? The Jaguars are 9-point favorites, according to BetMGM , and -525 on the moneyline. Baltimore is +400. The over-under is 42.5. Who's injured? Jaguars: Questionable — RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot), DE Travon Walker (rib). Ravens: Out — S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), QB Tyler Huntley (toe). Questionable — RB Adam Randall (neck), CB Nate Wiggins (stinger, illness). What's the series history between the Jaguars and Ravens? The Ravens are one of the few teams on which the Jaguars hold an edge, leading 13-11. The Jaguars won the first eight meetings and have been 5-11 since then, and 1-7 in Baltimore. They have split their last six meetings 3-3. Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Zay Jones (7) is celebrated by teammate cornerback Tyson Campbell (32) after scoring a two-point conversion during the fourth quarter of a regular season NFL football matchup Sunday, Nov. 27, 2022 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville. What happened the last time the Jaguars played the Ravens? Lamar Jackson passed for 171 yards and ran for 97 as the Ravens won 23-7 on Dec. 17, 2023, on a Sunday night game in Jacksonville. What's the key Jaguars-Ravens matchup? Jaguars defense vs. Ravens RB Derrick Henry Yes, it will take a village, or the entire defense to make sure that the Ravens don't get control of the game and try to keep it by battering the Yulee product at them. The Jaguars defense hasn't given up a 100-yard rusher in the last 24 games but Henry had eight of those against the Jags when he was with Tennessee, and in 15 career games vs. Jacksonville, he's churned out an All-Pro season: 1,584 yards, 16 touchdowns, and a 5.4 per-carry average. Jan 7, 2024; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans running back Derrick Henry (22) takes the field during the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguarsat Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-USA TODAY Sports The Jaguars have a history of holding Henry down when he's playing with a backup quarterback. In 2022, the Jags held Henry to 109 yards on 30 carries in a 20-16 victory that clinched the AFC South title , and the next year limited him to 38 yards in one game. But Henry still looks the part after 11 NFL seasons and is well on his way to another 1,000-yard season. The only way the Ravens win this game is with Henry dominating and the Jags' vaunted run defense needs its best effort -- without nose tackle DaVon Hamilton . What's notable about Jaguars vs. Ravens? The Jaguars will play their 17th Thursday night game in history and their seventh on the road. Jacksonville is 7-9 on Thursday nights and 2-4 on the road, but the last two have been victories, 19-3 over the New York Jets in 2022 and 31-24 over New Orleans in 2023. ... The Jaguars are 22-25 in games played in prime time, 4-10 on the road. ... The Jaguars are 13-2 in their last 15 regular-season games, the most in the NFL over that span, and have scored 20 or more points in in 13 games. Their +238 point differential during that span is the best in the NFL by 104 points over San Francisco. ... The Jags are 7-3 on the road under coach Liam Coen and are 2-1 vs. AFC North opponents. ... Last week's victory pushed Coen's record overall to 18-6 (.750), the highest winning percentage among active NFL coaches with 20 or more games. away.headline: Final injury report: Antonio Johnson gives Jaguars a spark Ravens aren't ready for
away.blurb: The Jaguars posted their final injury report against the Ravens. Antonio Johnson is good to go, even though he was a limited participant in practice this season. Then again, easing him back into action was probably the best course of action, so he's back at full strength, or as close to it, on Sunday Night Football. While Johnson is good to go, defensive end Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhaysul Tuten are listed as questionable. Head coach Liam Coen stated that Tuten will be a game-time decision . Offensive guard Ezra Cleveland was limited in practice due to knee and ankle injuries, but Coen says he'll suit up against the Ravens. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), and running back Chris Rodriguez also practiced on a limited basis but were cleared to play. With Johnson back in the fold, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will be able to get creative in an effort to overwhelm 2026 third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, who'll get the starting nod with Lamar Johnson and Tyler Huntley out for the season. Aside from Johnson, Jacksonville also has Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III at safety. The Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night. Although there's a chance running back Bhayshul Tuten won't suit up for the game, the Jags will get reinforcements on defense . Antonio Johnson will be back after missing the win over the Indianapolis Colts due to an ankle injury. Having him back will be huge since Jacksonville lost fellow safety Eric Murray and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the year. Antonio Johnson didn't appear in the Jaguars' final injury report vs. the Ravens It's worth noting that Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray also popped up on the injury report, but both of them are landed on the injured reserve list after season-ending injuries in the win over the Colts. You may also like: Walker Little is quietly turning doubters into believers Why having Antonio Johnson vs. the Ravens will be huge for the Jaguars Antonio Johnson had a breakout season in 2025, registering a career-best five interceptions and nine passes defensed. Meanwhile, Lane was just named Defensive Player of the Week after registering three passes defensed and returning an interception for a touchdown after picking up Daniel Jones. away.headline: Report: Jaguars Trade Urgency ‘Amplified’ After Injury
away.blurb: “The belief in league circles is that Jacksonville has been looking for interior DL help at the deadline. That need only amplifies with Hamilton out,” tweeted Fowler . The belief in league circles is Jacksonville has been looking for interior DL help at the deadline. That need only amplifies with Hamilton out. https://t.co/OqRZAiWkxw — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 2, 2026 The team had been linked to names like Moro Ojomo and Zach Sieler prior to the injury. Report: Jaguars Trade Urgency ‘Amplified' After Injury Unlock the latest Heavy on Jaguars news — direct to your inbox. The Jacksonville Jaguars are expected to be without defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn quad. With the trade deadline approaching, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN noted that the Jaguars' need for a defensive tackle has been amplified due to the injury. He also reported that the belief in league circles was that the team would explore upgrades on the line before the injury. Jacksonville Jaguars Ramping Up Search for Defensive Line Help John Shipley of Jaguars OnSI noted that the Jaguars needed to improve their pass rush, and that could have been in the form of a defensive lineman prior to the game. “Simply put, if the Jaguars struggle to impact Jones with their pass-rush on Sunday, then they will have to raise the urgency to add a pass-rusher at the deadline,” wrote Shipley on the Jaguars' need prior to Week 8. “Regardless of whether it is edge help or interior defensive line reinforcements, this game and matchup should tell the Jaguars how badly they need to add some help.” The issue now is that Hamilton was their best run-defending threat. They went from needing a pass-rushing interior lineman to a player who can impact the game in both the pass and run. So, they will either need to take a bigger swing or look to take multiple swings on the line. Shipley acknowledged the difference after the game. “Jacksonville was likely already in the market for a pocket-pushing three-technique who could make an impact on passing downs next to Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Arik Armstead, and Ruke Orhorhoro,” he added. “That is still a need, too. away.blurb: Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice Tuesday as the result of an ankle/foot injury. Tuten was also listed as a non-participant in the walkthrough on the practice field Monday, with that day's injury report being just an estimate. Rodriguez himself was limited in Tuesday's practice with a hand injury, but that doesn't take away from the fact that he would be the expected bell cow of the offense if Tuten can't play. Tuten has played a massive role in the offense through the first seven games, getting more carries than Rodriguez in every game but one (Week 6). Rodriguez has 45 carries for 209 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and three touchdowns this season, scoring two rushing touchdowns from 20+ yards out. This included a 28-yard touchdown in Week 8 against the Indianapolis Colts, with Rodriguez and Tuten each taking a step forward in giving the Jaguars the explosive rushing game they have been looking for. “It's there. I mean, just watch the film, like, it's there. There's been plenty of times where me and Bhayshul [Tuten] have talked, and we're like, man, if we just slowed down a little bit or had a bit more patience, or if we would have read it out all the way through the guy and not just reading our first read, but our second read, man, we'll have so many explosives," Rodriguez said about the explosive runs during the bye week. "And we talked about it today. There are so many yards that we left out there in this past game. home.headline: Final injury report: Antonio Johnson gives Jaguars a spark Ravens aren't ready for
home.blurb: The Jaguars posted their final injury report against the Ravens. Antonio Johnson is good to go, even though he was a limited participant in practice this season. Then again, easing him back into action was probably the best course of action, so he's back at full strength, or as close to it, on Sunday Night Football. While Johnson is good to go, defensive end Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhaysul Tuten are listed as questionable. Head coach Liam Coen stated that Tuten will be a game-time decision . Offensive guard Ezra Cleveland was limited in practice due to knee and ankle injuries, but Coen says he'll suit up against the Ravens. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), and running back Chris Rodriguez also practiced on a limited basis but were cleared to play. With Johnson back in the fold, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will be able to get creative in an effort to overwhelm 2026 third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, who'll get the starting nod with Lamar Johnson and Tyler Huntley out for the season. Aside from Johnson, Jacksonville also has Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III at safety. The Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night. Although there's a chance running back Bhayshul Tuten won't suit up for the game, the Jags will get reinforcements on defense . Antonio Johnson will be back after missing the win over the Indianapolis Colts due to an ankle injury. Having him back will be huge since Jacksonville lost fellow safety Eric Murray and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the year. Antonio Johnson didn't appear in the Jaguars' final injury report vs. the Ravens It's worth noting that Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray also popped up on the injury report, but both of them are landed on the injured reserve list after season-ending injuries in the win over the Colts. home.headline: Ravens injury report: 4 starters return to full practice for Week 9
home.blurb: Offensive linemen Vega Ioane and Ronnie Stanley, linebacker Roquan Smith, outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, and running back Justice Hill were all upgraded from limited to full participation on Baltimore's latest Week 9 injury report. The improvements provide some much-needed optimism for a Ravens team dealing with significant injuries during a short week. However, quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley remained out of practice, along with safety Jaylinn Hawkins. Defensive lineman Calais Campbell also did not participate, although his absence was designated as rest rather than an injury. *Fagnano's Monday estimated limited participation was separately confirmed. He does not appear on the Tuesday team graphic and was a full participant. Randall remains designated for return from injured reserve. Ioane's return to full participation is particularly significant after the rookie right guard dealt with an MCL sprain that limited his availability. He participated on a limited basis Monday before being upgraded Tuesday, giving Baltimore a potential boost along the interior offensive line. Stanley also returned to full participation after being limited Monday because of a combination of rest, toe and ankle issues. The Ravens still have questions elsewhere along the offensive line. Right tackle Roger Rosengarten remained limited with an ankle injury, while guard John Simpson was limited because of a back injury. Defensive tackle John Jenkins also remained limited with a knee injury. With undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano preparing to make his first NFL start against Jacksonville, Baltimore's offensive linemen will be particularly important. The Ravens allowed four sacks and struggled to produce consistently against Buffalo. Jackson did not practice Tuesday because of the right thumb injury he suffered against Buffalo. The two-time NFL MVP is expected to undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve, sidelining him for at least four games. Huntley also remained out with a turf toe injury. Coach Jesse Minter acknowledged Tuesday that the veteran backup could be an injured reserve candidate, potentially leaving Baltimore without its top two quarterbacks for an extended period. Minter has already named Fagnano the starter for Thursday's matchup. The rookie practiced Tuesday wearing a substantial brace on his right ankle after being listed as limited during Monday's estimated walkthrough. Smith had been limited because of a foot injury, while Hendrickson was managing finger and rib issues. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was a full participant for the second straight day despite being listed with a stinger, while safety Hawkins remained sidelined with a knee injury. Tight ends Mark Andrews and Matthew Hibner also practiced fully despite hand injuries. Running back Adam Randall, who has been designated to return from injured reserve, was a full participant as he continues working back from a neck injury. home.blurb: In the same report, Dan Graziano noted the Ravens will "work to solve the problem" with Jackson out for the time being and are "open to a number of ideas" at the quarterback spot with Jacoby Brissett cited as someone they could "look into" acquiring. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars. It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race. Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some of the options the Ravens are looking at include Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent. Jackson returned on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after missing three games then injured his thumb on his first pass attempt. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The Bears may not be eager to trade Bagent since Caleb Williams has already missed time this season, though they did get one quality start from Case Keenum during Williams' absence that might make head coach Ben Johnson comfortable if he had to step in. The Colts are reportedly open to trading Jonathan Taylor, but they still played him 38 offensive snaps and risked a potential injury in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew will remain the starter going forward and rookie Carson Beck will be the No. 2, leaving Brissett as the emergency third quarterback. home.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
home.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Breaking Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell says he has ‘full movement' of lower body after scary on-field injury An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Sunday’s Week 9 matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) and the Atlanta Falcons (3-5) comes with an unusual backdrop, as the teams meet at Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid for a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. The Bengals have won three in a row and sit in second place in the AFC North, a half-game behind the Steelers. The Falcons have won just three games and are two games under .500 but in the NFC South that is good enough to also be within a half-game of first. The Bengals arrive in Spain after surviving one of the wildest games last weekend, a 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans that required Cincinnati to erase multiple deficits. Tennessee jumped ahead 13-0, led 21-13 in the third quarter and was still up 29-23 during the fourth, but Joe Burrow repeatedly brought the Bengals back. He connected with Mike Gesicki for a 25-yard touchdown and later found Tee Higgins for an 18-yard score with 1:17 remaining to force overtime at 36-36. Burrow then finished the comeback himself, scrambling nine yards for the game-winning touchdown in overtime. He has been the driving force behind Cincinnati’s three-game winning streak, which also includes road victories over Miami and Baltimore. He has the Bengals’ offense averaging a stout 29.4 points per game. An inconsistent offense has plagued Atlanta all season and last Sunday was no exception. Yes, their game against Tampa was played in torrential and constant rain, but the Bucs weathered the storm and won 16-0. Atlanta was held to 224 total yards, committed four turnovers and possessed the ball for only 24:44 as Tampa Bay controlled the game on the ground. Heck, Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes…and did not complete a one. Michael Penix Jr. endured a particularly rough afternoon, throwing a career-high four interceptions, while the Falcons managed just 125 net passing yards and 99 rushing yards. Tampa Bay pounded Atlanta for 324 rushing yards, including 170 and a touchdown from Bucky Irving and another 140 from Kenny Gainwell . The recent history favors the Bengals, who lead the all-time series 10-5 and have won the last three meetings. The latest came in October 2022, when Burrow carved Atlanta apart for 481 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 35-17 Cincinnati victory. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Falcons odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup in Madrid | Cincy Jungle Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Cincinnati Bengals Community Cincy Jungle November 5, 2026 Cincy Jungle Notifications Notifications Sections News By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds Cincinnati Bengals Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand News By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Cincinnati Bengals odds Oddsmakers expect a high-scoring affair in Spain. The Cincinnati Bengals needed a spectacular performance from Joe Burrow to escape with an overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but oddsmakers aren’t expecting the same kind of offensive fireworks when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons next weekend. Still, with the Bengals’ defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta, with the Bengals listed at -225 on the moneyline and the Falcons at +188. The opening over/under was set at 49.5 points. The latest FanDuel odds show Cincinnati remaining a 3.5-point favorite, although the price has shifted to -102 for the Bengals and -120 for the Falcons. The Bengals’ moneyline has moved to -184, while Atlanta’s stands at +154. The over/under has increased by one point to 50.5. The Bengals enter the matchup following a wild 43-36 overtime victory over Tennessee that featured five touchdown passes and three interceptions from Burrow, who ultimately delivered the winning score by scrambling nine yards around left end for just the second offensive overtime touchdown in franchise history. But while Cincinnati’s offense once again demonstrated its ability to put points on the scoreboard, the defense raised serious questions. The Bengals surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered Sunday’s game with just one victory, delivering a performance that looked disturbingly similar to the defensive struggles that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Atlanta, meanwhile, is coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that did not complete a single pass. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn’t find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. away.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation
away.blurb: Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Fellow safety Jordan Battle was also limited again with a shoulder injury, but he's been playing through that issue in outings over the last few weeks. On the Titans' side of things, starting defensive tackle John Franklin-Meyers (groin) upgraded to limited and starting receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice for a second-straight day. Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday. He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine. Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks. Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well. "Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play." Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role. "PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)." Cincinnati has a light practice on Friday. Published Oct 29, 2026 | Modified Oct 29, 2026 RUSSELL HELTMAN Russ Heltman is on the Bearcats and Bengals beat for On SI. away.headline: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans
away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. home.headline: Bengals reveal who would've missed their first practice ahead of Week 9 matchup against Falcons hours after landing in Madrid
home.blurb: The Cincinnati Bengals released their first injury report ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bengals arrived in Madrid, Spain early Wednesday morning and did not practice after landing, but did indicate who would've missed practice. The big name to monitor this week is cornerback DJ Turner II (heel). Turner, who left during Sunday's win against the Tennessee Titans , is officially day-to-day with his heel injury and would not have practiced Wednesday. That he made the trip to Spain at all is a promising sign for him to potentially play against Atlanta. Still, he'll likely need a full practice later in the week for Cincinnati to give him the green light. Defense end Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) would've also been a non-participant Wednesday. Johnson also left the Titans game and did not return, but like Turner, he is in Spain with a chance to suit up Sunday morning. It would be a significant loss if either Turner or Johnson weren't able to play. Without Turner, the Bengals would likely start both DJ Ivey and Josh Newton alongside Week 1 starter Dax Hill. Neither Ivey nor Newton are trustworthy starters for an entire game, and even Hill had his fair share of struggles against Tennessee last week. Johnson is fourth in the DE rotation which just lost rookie Cashius Howell , the No. 3, to the Reserve/Injured list this week. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen would have gotten his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle would've been limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. The Falcons had a walkthrough Wednesday, making this injury report an estimation as well. DE Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Devine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) all missed Atlanta's Week 8 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to their respective injuries. Bowman would've been a full participant, and Deablo and Robinson would've been limited. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) would've been the lone Falcon to miss practice. home.blurb: "Asked about Pearce, Stefanski said the Falcons are pleased with where he is in terms of being football ready," wrote team reporter Tori McElhaney . The Colts just completed their annual beatdown at the hands of the Jaguars and are hoping home has some better results. The Cowboys are licking their own wounds and will be in fight mode to save their season. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Cowboys all the love as the Colts are 5.5-point underdogs. The money line is +220 and the over/under is 52.5. What is there to say? Going on the road against the Jaguars has been the Colts' kryptonite. Before things kicked off, it didn't seem like this was the year the losing streak was going to end. All that game ended was a few more players' careers as Colts. Turnovers, missed tackles, and a team that looks like it has thrown in the towel was on the field this week. It was 35-0 before the Colts decided to score. That's all you really need to know about this one. Dallas seemed to have their high-scoring affair under wraps with less than four minutes left in the fourth. Up ten wasn't enough, however, as the Cardinals scored a game-tying touchdown with ten seconds left. They gave the Cowboys a gift by missing the extra point and sending this one into overtime. Both teams got a possession in overtime, but the Cardinals got the last laugh with a game-winning field goal. Neither team is feeling good about their season. Dallas still has hope though. Expect Lucas Oil to be full of Cowboys fans as they travel well, and the Colts fans might have already thrown in the towel. If the Colts are going to get things right, it has to be this one. If not here, it might not happen this year at all.

(2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The bigger issues for Indianapolis are on the offensive side of the ball where the Colts average just 20.1 points per game. Yes, it seemed obvious the Colts were waving the white flag following midweek trades of DeForest Buckner and Quentin Nelson but to make sure there was no doubt of their intentions, they endured a smack from Jacksonville on Sunday, 42-7. The Jaguars led 28-0 at halftime and finished with 366 total yards, while the Colts’ offensive woes were on full display turning the ball over three times and amassing a mere 243 yards. Daniel Jones endured a particularly rough afternoon, finishing 19-of-28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, including a 92-yard pick-six, before Anthony Richardson replaced him late. Reports Monday indicated that Jones is expected to remain the starter against Dallas, with Richardson staying in the backup role. Sunday’s game is beyond a must-win for Dallas if they are to continue to entertain any hopes of even competing for a playoff spot. The Colts’ offense has been pedestrian on its better days, but the Cowboys have made even bad offenses look elite. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys reunite with practice squad RB after preseason stint
away.blurb: Although Javonte Williams has had impressive touchdown production, the Dallas Cowboys have struggled to find consistency in the running game during the 2026 season. Dallas has the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (94.1) despite being tied for the NFL's third-most rushing touchdowns (10) headed into Week 9's matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. A rushing unit that already struggles would be in deep water if Williams were to miss any time due to injury. Tyler Goodson has shown some promise but Dallas doesn't have any notable options behind him after parting ways with Emari Demercado. So as a result, the Cowboys are bringing a familiar face back to the practice squad if running back depth becomes an issue moving forward. Cowboys Sign RB Jashaun Corbin to Practice Squad The Cowboys have signed running back Jashaun Corbin to the practice squad, per reports from Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com. Corbin spent some time with Dallas during training camp and appeared in the team's preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints when he tallied three carries for 14 yards. It's clear the coaching staff likes his potential, as they are now reuniting with him a little over two months later. Corbin also spent time with the Atlanta Falcons during the 2025 preseason, finishing that three-game slate with 18 carries for 59 yards. Corbin played college football at both Texas A&M and Florida State before going undrafted in 2022. He signed a deal with the New York Giants and appeared in six games with the team in 2023. He played mostly on special teams but posted one carry for one yard and three catches for 12 yards. Coach Shane Steichen is resisting suggestions that the Colts hold him out or limit his exposure before the deadline. Taylor did not practice Wednesday, as has been routine under Steichen. He's fourth in the NFL in carries (148), tied for third in rushing touchdowns (eight) and eighth in rushing yards (610). In addition to Caleb Downs, P.J. Locke started the week in concussion protocol and Jalen Thompson remains out. Not much has gone right in the first half of the season for the Indianapolis Colts, who will carry the burden of a four-game losing streak and the weight of roster roulette when they host the Cowboys on Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys (3-5) blew a 17-3 second-half lead and handed the Cardinals a 33-30 win in a game that underscored two ongoing issues: a sputtering running game and a defense that's prone to being torched for big plays. Dallas has lost three of its past four games but stands only a game back of the New York Giants in the win column in the NFC East. Indianapolis (2-6) has traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson (to the Seattle Seahawks) and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (to the San Francisco 49ers), and reportedly rejected at least one offer for running back Jonathan Taylor. Wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, and the Colts are considering their options with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching. "He's on our football team and he's excited for this opportunity to go play. He wants to go win this game," Steichen said. If ever there was a moment for the Colts to polish their most valuable trade asset, this would be the week. Dallas is last in the NFL against the run, allowing 152.8 rushing yards per game. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has five of the Cowboys' 15 sacks and has made key plays, but he said no player on the defense is celebrating personal success. "We're the problem. In Week 8, the Dallas Cowboys were the one team that really hurt Survivor players, as they lost as a touchdown favorite at home against a frisky Arizona Cardinals team. Unfortunately for the SI Betting team, Dallas was one of the two teams that we gave out for last week's picks. NFL Week 8 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Dallas Cowboys (L) On the bright side for the team, the Cincinnati Bengals held on in overtime to beat the Tennessee Titans, avoiding an 0-2 week when it comes to these picks. MacMillan is getting the chance to buy back in so we can offer some differing opinions in Week 9 and upsets across the NFL in the last few weeks have decimated many Survivor Pools. In Week 9, our team is looking to two teams that are favored by six or more points, including Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs after a tough loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. The Chiefs may not be as explosive as they once were, but on their home field they'll cruise past the Jets and help us advance our survivor entries to Week 10. – Iain MacMillan Dallas Cowboys I know the Dallas Cowboys and their terrible defense absolutely crushed Survivor Players (including our own Iain MacMillan) in Week 8, but I’m willing to go back to them on the road in a must-win game against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. The NFC North is crowded with the Lions sitting third despite having but two losses. Miami is in the cellar in the AFC East. Lets get the obvious out of the way. The difference between these teams is substantial: Detroit is averaging 29.0 points and an NFL-best 395.4 yards per game, while Miami is averaging only 16.7 points and 290.0 yards. Detroit’s latest victory was arguably its most impressive of the season, a 19-15 win over the previously unbeaten Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field last Sunday. The Lions trailed 7-6 at halftime before Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 30-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Minnesota regained the lead at 15-12 with 8:44 remaining, but Jared Goff responded by directing a seven-play, 69-yard drive and finding Jameson Williams for the go-ahead seven-yard touchdown with 4:35 left. Goff finished 18-of-25 for 176 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown and Williams caught four passes for 70 yards including the decisive score. The victory came at a cost, however, as linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury and was listed as doubtful on the early Week 9 injury information. The Dolphins are coming off a game that typified their frustrating season, blowing a 13-3 halftime lead in a 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Malik Willis and the Miami offense were in control early, but New England erupted for 21 unanswered second-half points, including touchdown passes of 43 and 48 yards from Drake Maye , to turn the game around. Miami finally answered when Willis connected with rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. for a 35-yard touchdown with 2:04 remaining, but the Dolphins failed on the ensuing two-point conversion and New England recovered the onside kick. Willis finished 21-of-32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception but was sacked five times, while Miami managed only 269 total yards and 74 on the ground. Although the Lions and Dolphins meet infrequently, their most recent games have been surprisingly competitive. Miami leads the all-time regular-season series 8-5, but Detroit won three straight meetings from 2010 through 2018 before Miami answered with a 31-27 victory at Ford Field in 2022. That most recent meeting was an offensive showcase: Tua Tagovailoa threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, Tyreek Hill piled up 188 receiving yards and the Dolphins rallied from a 27-17 deficit to win, despite Goff throwing for 321 yards. The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. After splitting their first four games, the Lions have found their footing with three straight wins. Detroit hung 45 points on the Cardinals in Arizona, edged the Packers 20-17 coming out of its bye, and then handed Minnesota its first loss of the season at Ford Field. The Lions are a pristine 4-0 at home but just 1-2 on the road, and this is their first road game since that Week 5 win in Arizona. Meanwhile, the Dolphins opened the Jeff Hafley era 0-5 before finally breaking through with a 28-25 win over the Jets in Week 7. They couldn't build on it, falling 24-19 at home to the New England Patriots last week, and Miami is now 0-3 at Hard Rock Stadium this season. Say what you want about the Dolphins, but their last four games have been decided by a touchdown or less. Lions vs. Dolphins Kickoff, Weather, TV, Streaming Info Kickoff is Sunday at 1:00 PM ET at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. The game will air on CBS, with streaming available on Fox One and NFL+. In Canada, DAZN carries every NFL game through NFL Game Pass. The weather forecast for Week 9's game calls for sunny skies and no chance of rain, with temperatures in the mid-20s at kickoff. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends The visiting Lions are 7.0-point road favourites with a -355 money line . The home Dolphins are placed at +280 on the money line, and the total sits at 50.5. Detroit Lions @ Miami Dolphins This season, Detroit has been one of the most explosive offences in football, averaging 29.0 points and 395.4 yards per game, and the over has hit in five of its seven contests. Jahmyr Gibbs entered Week 8 averaging 103.3 rushing yards per game as one of the early front-runners for NFL Offensive Player of the Year, and Jared Goff hadn't thrown an interception through six games before succumbing to the pressure of Minnesota's blitz-happy defence and tossing a pick. 2026/27 NFL - Awards AP Offensive Player of the Year The surprise has been the defence, which held Green Bay to 17 points and Minnesota to 15 in back-to-back weeks. Still, the Lions have been a tough team to back as a favourite, going 1-3-1 against the spread when laying points entering last week. As for the Dolphins, Malik Willis has given them some life with his legs, but the offence ranks near the bottom of the league at 16.7 points per game. Willis entered last week with just four touchdown passes against four interceptions, and Miami's defence has generated the fewest sacks in the NFL while allowing 25.9 points per game. That said, Willis has multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games, so perhaps he's showing some signs of life as a passer. With Detroit's offence facing a defence that can't get home, siding with the Lions on the road makes sense, though a touchdown is a lot to lay for a team that has struggled to cover as a favourite. The over is worth a look as well, given how often Lions games have cleared the number. NFL Player Odds and Props Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 100.5 rushing yards Gibbs has been the engine of this Lions offence, entering Week 8 averaging 103.3 rushing yards per game on one of the league's heaviest workloads. Miami's defence has struggled to get off the field all season, and if Detroit builds a lead, the Lions will lean on Gibbs to bleed the clock in the Florida heat. The one thing to monitor is the shoulder injury that kept him out of practice ahead of the Vikings game, but with the Lions very concentrated in the run game, Gibbs should have ample opportunity to get above the century mark against the Dolphins. Malik Willis OVER 29.5 rushing yards We went with this prop last week, and Willis tallied just two yards on the ground. That lack of output was an anomaly, and we're going back to the well this week. He is the key to any Dolphins upset, and Willis' legs are clearly his most dangerous weapon. Willis is at his best when he's moving, and he ran for over 100 yards and two touchdowns across his two games heading into last week. Miami's offence is built around designed runs, zone reads and scrambles, and that shouldn't change against a Lions defence that has been aggressive in coverage. If the Dolphins fall behind, Willis will be forced to create on his own, which usually means more yards with his legs. Goff has been efficient and careful with the ball, throwing for 303 yards and two touchdowns against Green Bay and keeping the turnovers to a minimum. Amon-Ra St. Brown set a new career high in receiving yards in that game, and with Gibbs carrying the ground game and Jameson Williams stretching the field, this offence has a weapon at every level. Sam LaPorta has been quieter of late, but he remains a reliable red zone option for Goff. Production for the Lions was muted against a tough Minnesota defence as Goff passed for just 176 yards, but Gibbs was the alpha here with 153 yards and a touchdown on the ground and Williams adding a touchdown on four grabs for 70 yards. The bigger story over the last two weeks has been the defence. After giving up 17 touchdowns through the first four games, the Lions have tightened up considerably, holding two NFC North rivals to 32 combined points. Facing a Dolphins offence averaging just 16.7 points per game, Detroit's defence has a chance to keep that momentum going. Running back Ollie Gordon II has been the most consistent piece of this offence, rushing for 339 yards and four touchdowns on 72 carries heading into last week, when he put up 69 yards as a running back that lacks any receiving profile. Still, the Dolphins will need him to keep Detroit's offence on the sideline. Willis found a connection with rookie Caleb Douglas in the win over the Jets, while Malik Washington and tight end Greg Dulcich gave Willis options underneath. The problem is consistency, as Miami has not been able to string together complete performances through the air. It's to be expected for such a young team that's trying to find an identity as well as players for the future who will be around long-term as they rebuild into a contender. Defensively, Zach Sieler anchors the interior, but the Dolphins simply can't pressure the quarterback, and that's a dangerous combination against a passer like Goff. If Miami can't make Detroit uncomfortable, its best hope is controlling the clock with Gordon and Willis and keeping this one close into the fourth quarter. away.blurb: "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time," the team said in a statement. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

away.blurb: The Lions did not officially hold a practice on Wednesday, opting instead for a walk-through, but provided an estimated practice report listing four players (including linebacker Jack Campbell) as non-participants and five as limited. Safety Brian Branch (concussion protocol) was surprisingly ruled a limited participant, along with safety Kerby Joseph (knee), linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe), running back Jacob Saylors (neck), and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib). The new injury to watch is St. Brown's, one of the team's best players. He was not known to have a rib injury, but the fact that he was listed as limited is a positive sign. St. Brown, who was a non-participant in last week's Monday practice because of an ankle injury, caught seven passes for 46 yards in the team's 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings . Center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback DJ Reed (hip) and defensive end DJ Wonnum (concussion protocol) were all listed as non-participants. All absences were expected according to statements from coach Dan Campbell earlier in the week. Campbell said Tuesday on 97.1 The Ticket that he expected Joseph, who hasn't played since Week 6 of last season, to rejoin the scout team this week.
