home.headline: Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown limited ahead of Dolphins matchup
home.blurb: The Lions did not officially hold a practice on Wednesday, opting instead for a walk-through, but provided an estimated practice report listing four players (including linebacker Jack Campbell) as non-participants and five as limited. Safety Brian Branch (concussion protocol) was surprisingly ruled a limited participant, along with safety Kerby Joseph (knee), linebacker Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe), running back Jacob Saylors (neck), and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib). The new injury to watch is St. Brown's, one of the team's best players. He was not known to have a rib injury, but the fact that he was listed as limited is a positive sign. St. Brown, who was a non-participant in last week's Monday practice because of an ankle injury, caught seven passes for 46 yards in the team's 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings . Center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback DJ Reed (hip) and defensive end DJ Wonnum (concussion protocol) were all listed as non-participants. All absences were expected according to statements from coach Dan Campbell earlier in the week. Campbell said Tuesday on 97.1 The Ticket that he expected Joseph, who hasn't played since Week 6 of last season, to rejoin the scout team this week. Among those listed were Jack Campbell, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed, Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph, and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Branch's limited designation is worth monitoring after he and Wonnum were both ruled out of Sunday's game with concussions following a helmet-to-helmet collision. His progression through the league's concussion protocol will be important as Detroit prepares for Miami. Joseph also appeared on the report as limited with a knee injury, although Dan Campbell said on his Tuesday radio appearance that the safety will not play against the Dolphins . The Lions continue taking a cautious approach as the safety works his way back toward game action. St. Brown's appearance with a rib injury is another situation to watch. While he was listed as limited, Wednesday's designation alone does not indicate whether his availability for Sunday is in jeopardy. The team's own report spells it out: "The Lions conducted a walkthrough on Wednesday. Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations." Detroit's situation should become clearer once the team holds a full practice. That makes Thursday and Friday particularly important, especially for players dealing with concussions and those hoping to return from injuries suffered against Minnesota. After missing last Sunday's loss to the New England Patriots , left guard Kadyn Proctor returned to practice Wednesday, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley announced, as the rookie continues progressing through concussion protocol. The Dolphins' rushing attack took a hit without Proctor in the lineup Without Proctor last week, the Dolphins started Jarrett Kingston at left guard, and their rushing attack suffered. After surpassing 100 rushing yards in each of their previous five games, Miami managed just 74 yards on the ground in its 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Getting Proctor back would provide a significant boost as Miami prepares to face a Detroit offense that can put up points quickly. at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South, but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.source: New Orleans Saints On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards. For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September . Initially expected to return in mid-December, Banks could reclaim his starting role once medically cleared, giving the Saints additional protection up front. New Orleans also welcomed back Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State. The rookie wide receiver participated on a limited basis Wednesday after missing the entire season to this point with a hamstring injury suffered during training camp . Although his availability for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, Tyson's return represents another encouraging development for a Saints offense looking to improve its passing attack. The New Orleans Saints received encouraging injury updates Wednesday as left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns . Meanwhile, Cleveland could be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , who entered the NFL's concussion protocol Wednesday after reporting symptoms following Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . Watson initially passed concussion evaluations and finished the game but reported symptoms Monday night, putting his availability against New Orleans in question. If Watson cannot play, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season. Watson has started all eight games for Cleveland this season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite his efficiency, the Browns have struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the NFL with just 17.4 points per game. The second-year left tackle has progressed considerably faster than initially expected, returning more than a month ahead of schedule. The Saints now have a two-week window to activate Banks from injured reserve, potentially providing a significant boost to an offensive line that has struggled in his absence. Backup left tackle Asim Richards has experienced difficulties adjusting to coach Kellen Moore's offensive scheme while filling in for Banks. With Banks and Tyson progressing toward their respective returns and Cleveland potentially facing a quarterback change, Sunday's matchup could feature a considerably different outlook for both teams than initially anticipated. home.headline: Saints Get Major Injury Boost as Browns Face Quarterback Uncertainty
home.source: New Orleans Saints On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards. For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September . Initially expected to return in mid-December, Banks could reclaim his starting role once medically cleared, giving the Saints additional protection up front. New Orleans also welcomed back Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State. The rookie wide receiver participated on a limited basis Wednesday after missing the entire season to this point with a hamstring injury suffered during training camp . Although his availability for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, Tyson's return represents another encouraging development for a Saints offense looking to improve its passing attack. The New Orleans Saints received encouraging injury updates Wednesday as left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns . Meanwhile, Cleveland could be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , who entered the NFL's concussion protocol Wednesday after reporting symptoms following Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . Watson initially passed concussion evaluations and finished the game but reported symptoms Monday night, putting his availability against New Orleans in question. If Watson cannot play, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season. Watson has started all eight games for Cleveland this season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite his efficiency, the Browns have struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the NFL with just 17.4 points per game. The second-year left tackle has progressed considerably faster than initially expected, returning more than a month ahead of schedule. The Saints now have a two-week window to activate Banks from injured reserve, potentially providing a significant boost to an offensive line that has struggled in his absence. Backup left tackle Asim Richards has experienced difficulties adjusting to coach Kellen Moore's offensive scheme while filling in for Banks. With Banks and Tyson progressing toward their respective returns and Cleveland potentially facing a quarterback change, Sunday's matchup could feature a considerably different outlook for both teams than initially anticipated. home.blurb: Saints head coach Kellen Moore told reporters on Monday that the team is still working through a decision on opening Tyson's 21-day return window, which would begin if Tyson makes his return to practice. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . The New Orleans Saints are getting closer to seeing the debut of their first-round pick. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice on Wednesday, according to Saints reporter Nick Underhill . New Orleans selected the Arizona State product with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury during training camp landed Tyson on the injured reserve list. Despite having a 2-5 record, the Saints still have the opportunity to make the playoffs in a weak NFC South division. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Deshaun Watson's status in doubt as Browns travel to face Saints
home.blurb: But Watson is in concussion protocol and might be unavailable when the Browns visit the New Orleans Saints (2-5) on Sunday. "Last year I was able to see what I needed to see, feel different things during the games and understand what I needed to get better at," Sanders said. "Just (have to) go out there and trust my teammates, trust the game plan and do everything I can." "We've got to go out and score points right away," quarterback Tyler Shough said. "We have to do a better job as a whole offense. I think we're trending in the right direction." The Saints' offense should receive a boost when their last two No. 1 draft choices -- wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (2026) and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (2025) -- return to game action as soon as this week. Both are on injured reserve but returned to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Tyson has a hamstring injury and Banks has been sidelined with an ankle injury. Watson returned from a nearly two-year absence due to a ruptured Achilles to lead five fourth-quarter, game-winning drives for the Browns (5-3). Backup Shedeur Sanders took all the reps at quarterback in practice Wednesday, but head coach Todd Monken still hoped Watson could play Sunday. "It's not ideal for any player to go through a week and not practice and then go play," Monken said. "We know that, but every situation is different." Sanders started Cleveland's last seven games last season as a rookie fifth-round draft choice and the team went 3-4 in those games. Whoever starts at quarterback will try to help the Browns get off to a better start than they have been. Those comebacks Watson engineered were necessary because the Browns have made a habit of falling behind early, getting outscored 65-13 in the first quarter. "Luckily our guys have continued to fight, I'll give them that," Monken said. "But it's not the optimal way to win." The Saints have had similar problems starting games -- getting outscored 44-6 in the first quarter -- but they haven't been able to come back as successfully as Cleveland has. New Orleans had its bye last week, during which head coach Kellen Moore fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti. The Saints rank 28th in the NFL in rushing offense (86.0 yards per game), and they had just 18 yards on 17 rushes in their last game, a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris. A week earlier, though, they rushed for a season-high 175 yards on 38 carries in a 34-27 road victory against the New York Giants. "Running the football is always an important aspect," Moore said. "We've got to control the line of scrimmage and be physical running the football. We've seen instances of that, but not enough of it." Moore, who oversees the offense and calls the plays, said Paganetti's responsibilities have been distributed within the offensive staff. The Giants are coming off a bye in Week 8 after a stunning 27-21 overtime victory as 10-point underdogs on the road over the Houston Texans . On the other sideline, the Eagles are off to their worst (2-6) in more than a quarter century, with their current six-game losing streak being the longest since President Barack Obama was reelected for a second term in 2012. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Giants vs Eagles Week 9 predictions, staff standings Art Stapleton: 4-2-1 Dave Rivera: 3-3-1 Bert Bainbridge: 2-4-1 Chris Iseman : 2-4-1 Bob Jordan: 2-4-1 Brian Marron: 2-4-1 Mike Dougherty: 1-5-1 Can the Giants continue their stranglehold on the East or will the Birds losing ways finally come to an end with an upset at home over Big Blue? Art Stapleton The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 23 Here's why: John Harbaugh's team had a great bye week, with Dallas' stunning overtime defeat to Arizona increasing Big Blue's lead in the NFC East without even playing. QB J.J. McCarthy was outstanding in his first start against the Texans, clicking downfield with WR Malik Nabers, who had his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since Tom Coughlin was head coach in 2013, and they have not scored an offensive TD there in a win since their Super Bowl season of 2011. It's time for the streak to end. Bert Bainbridge The pick: Giants 30, Eagles 17 Here's why: No one thought this would be the reality at the midway point of the season with the Giants in the driver seat in the NFC East and the Eagles in free fall mode. Fresh off a bye, the G-Men go into Philadelphia and defeat the Birds at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 years. The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are spiraling as the key injuries continue to mount, especially on offense. The Giants are the better team right now, and are fresh off of a bye week. Expect Big Blue to earn a relatively comfortable win. The pick: Giants 34, Eagles 20 Here's why: The Eagles are a mess right now and that's a big reason why the Giants are in prime position to win the NFC East. The pick: Giants 23, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are going nowhere this season, and with the Cowboys and Commanders not showing to be real threats in the NFC East at this point, John Harbaugh and the Giants are seizing the opportunity. Mike Dougherty The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 17 Here's why: After six consecutive losses, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni vowed his team would keep fighting. Those are not words usually heard in early November. A high-intensity start by the Giants should remove any drama from this one. The pick: Giants 22, Eagles 19 Here's why: J.J. McCarthy may not be Y.A. Tittle but doesn't have to be with Harbaugh's spiffy after-a-bye record (15–3, best among modern era head coaches with at least 10 games). When Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, the Giants, unwilling to give up on the season, traded for J.J. McCarthy, the former first-round pick who was languishing on the Vikings ' bench as the No. 3 QB. They were buyers, and they still might be as they're rumored to be in the running for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor by the Nov. 10 deadline. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets Contrast that to when Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was presumably lost for the season due to blood clots. The Eagles turned the position over to their No. 3 QB (at the start of the season) in Tanner McKee, to mixed results. And it's believed that they're sellers at the deadline after already trading A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens for future draft picks. As for the Giants, who are in first place in the NFC East at 4-2-1, McCarthy has shined in his five quarters of action. He threw for 252 yards in a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans in Houston on Oct. 25. The week before, McCarthy nearly led a comeback against the Saints when he replaced Jameis Winston and threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter. away.blurb: Fixed rate energy plans available • Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard being limited isn't new either. • QB Jalen Hurts (IR, season over) : Hurts is out indefinitely with blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee took over initially as the team's starting quarterback, but he will be replaced by Joe Milton this Sunday. • RB Tank Bigsby (IR, eligible to return at any time) : Bigsby suffered an injury Week 4 against the Rams that required core muscle surgery. He will likely return this season, but could miss up to two months. • RB Will Shipley (IR, eligible to return after Week 9) : Shipley suffered a Lisfranc injury and will be out a while. Shipley is the Eagles' best RB in pass protection, but he only has 57 yards on 20 carries this season. • RB Dameon Pierce (IR, eligible to return after Week 12) : The Eagles' top four RBs are all injured. • LB Tremaine Edmunds : Edmunds played for five seasons in Buffalo and then the last three in Chicago before signing with the Giants in free agency. He has had 100 or more tackles in all eight seasons of his career. In 2025 he had 112 tackles, 4 INTs, and 9 pass breakups. Through 6 games in 2026, he had 50 tackles and 2 sacks. He suffered a torn chest muscle and is out for the season. Another major loss. • RS Gunner Olszewski : Olszewski tore his Achilles during OTAs. With Austin and Olszewski both out the Giants' primary retirn specialist has been Charlie Jones. Your next job? The Eagles and Giants have both lost their starting quarterbacks for the season. The Philadelphia Eagles have lost six straight games, partly because they have been ravaged by injuries and other losses, most notably Jalen Hurts' season being ended by blood clots and Lane Johnson's surprise retirement. The New York Giants have had major injuries as well, losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and star edge rusher Brian Burns for the season. However, they have weathered their injuries better than the Eagles have. Here's the Eagles-Giants injury report, with analysis. • The usual players who haven't practiced the last few weeks still aren't practicing. • Jake Elliott popped up on the injury report today. He had a long kicking session during the media-attended portion of the practice, and seemed to be striking the ball fine. Maybe he got hurt later in practice? NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game Skip to main content SI.COM New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice. Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago. At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.” Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans. Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury. If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game. "I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray). "So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll." While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia. Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring. Washington also got back in the win column, improving to 2-4-1 with a 27-10 victory over Philadelphia that snapped a three-game winless streak. For more picks across the full slate, check out our NFL predictions for this week's games. Rams vs. Commanders Kickoff, Weather, TV, Streaming Info Kickoff is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland. The game airs on FOX and streams on FOX One and NFL+ where available. In Canada, Rams vs. Commanders can be streamed nationwide on DAZN through NFL Game Pass. Early forecasts suggest temperatures in the 15C range with mostly sunny skies and light winds. NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends Los Angeles enters as a 5.5-point favourite and -255 on the moneyline , while Washington is listed at +210 to win outright. The total is set at 47.5 points. Los Angeles Rams @ Washington Commanders The Rams are 4-4 against the spread and have won three of their past five games, including consecutive victories over Las Vegas and the Chargers. Washington is 4-3 ATS after last week's convincing win over Philadelphia. Los Angeles also won the most recent meeting between these teams, beating Washington 28-20 in December 2023. NFL Player Odds and Props Los Angeles Rams Kyren Williams Anytime Touchdown (-140) Williams has rushed for 548 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 4.9 yards per carry, and he has found the end zone in consecutive games. Washington enters with an injury-depleted defensive front, giving Williams another favourable opportunity to see touches around the goal line. Puka Nacua Over 91.5 Receiving Yards (-118) Nacua leads Los Angeles with 56 receptions for 565 yards and three touchdowns. He has cleared this number twice in five games, and his target share could increase with Davante Adams sidelined. That should keep Nacua heavily involved in a Rams passing game that may have to lean on its top receiver even more than usual. Jayden Daniels Over 35.5 Rushing Yards (-118) Daniels' mobility remains one of the most dangerous elements of Washington's offence, particularly when passing plays break down. He recently returned from a dislocated elbow, but with several offensive starters unavailable, the Commanders may need him to create more with his legs against the Rams. Stefon Diggs Anytime Touchdown (+200) Diggs provides Washington with an experienced receiving threat following Terry McLaurin's season-ending knee injury. His route-running and ability to create separation should make him an important option for Daniels, particularly in the red zone. The Rams enter Sunday on consecutive victories after beating the Chargers 24-9 last week. Matthew Stafford threw for 157 yards and a touchdown in the win, while Kyren Williams added 56 rushing yards and a score. Los Angeles has begun to generate some momentum after an uneven first half of the season, but injuries remain a significant concern. Stafford is dealing with soreness in his throwing arm, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve following hamstring surgery. The Rams are also dealing with several injuries on defence. Myles Garrett is recovering from knee surgery, defensive tackle Poona Ford is out for the season with a triceps injury, and cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson suffered back and shoulder injuries, respectively, against the Chargers. Tight end Colby Parkinson is also questionable with a rib injury. Los Angeles will need to protect Stafford and maintain the defensive intensity it showed against the Chargers despite a growing list of unavailable players. Washington enters Week 9 with some momentum of its own after a 27-10 victory over Philadelphia. Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown without an interception as the Commanders ended their three-game winless streak. Like the Rams, however, Washington is dealing with substantial injury problems. Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a knee injury, while defensive tackle Daron Payne is also done for the year because of a foot injury. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil, defensive linemen Javon Kinlaw and Jer'Zhan Newton, and running back Jeremy McNichols are all on injured reserve. Newton has entered his practice-return window, while Daniels and Stefon Diggs have recently returned to action. The depleted defensive front could be particularly important against Kyren Williams and the Rams' running game. Washington will also need to keep Daniels protected against a Los Angeles pass rush capable of creating pressure when opponents are forced into obvious passing situations. away.headline: Los Angeles Rams: Get devastating news on $51 million standout
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams standout cornerback Jaylen Watson suffered a dislocated right shoulder in Week 3, which caused him to miss Week 4. Watson returned in Week 5 and has since worn a shoulder harness/brace. Unfortunately, the big-name free-agent acquisition suffered a shoulder injury during the third quarter of Week 8 and headed to the locker room for further examination. He was initially listed as questionable before being downgraded to out. The Los Angeles Rams get devastating news on $51 million standout During Wednesday’s press conference, Sean McVay provided a devastating injury update on Jaylen Watson , as reported by Greg Beacham of The Associated Press. McVay said Watson is expected to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery and will soon land on injured reserve. He finished his 2026 campaign with 24 tackles, two tackles for loss, one interception, and nine pass deflections across seven games. He also allowed a 50% completion rate, 261 passing yards, two touchdowns, and a 78.9 passer rating. Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr . are expected to take on expanded roles. Wallace has served as the No. 3 cornerback this season, totaling one interception and five pass deflections across eight games and six starts while averaging 73% of defensive snaps. Forbes has served as the No. 4 cornerback, totaling two pass deflections across eight games while averaging 25% of the snaps. Meanwhile, the Rams will likely promote either Damarion “Pepe” Williams or Cam Lampkin from the practice squad to the active roster. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. They're on the heels of a massive win over the rival Kansas City Chiefs that puts them in first place in the AFC West. The 28-24 win over the Chiefs also puts Denver in the hunt for home-field advantage. Yes, it's only eight games, but after the gauntlet the Broncos have faced, sitting at 6-2 and where they are is impressive. Now come the Carolina Panthers, who just got trucked on Thursday Night Football by the Green Bay Packers. As a result, the Panthers fired their defensive coordinator. Since Carolina plays in the NFC South, it leads the division at 3-4 and will be highly motivated to get back on track at home this Sunday. Denver is currently the -3-point road favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -118. Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Don't fall into the "trap" Sean Payton owns the NFC South. Dating back to his New Orleans Saints days, he knows the division and how to beat these teams. However, the Broncos have historically struggled in the early games on the East Coast. On top of that, Denver is coming off a brutal stretch of games and is on the heels of a ginormous win. Not to mention, the bye is after this Sunday's game. It's natural to take the foot off the gas and think, "We got this." In other words, the "trap game." Don't fall into that trap. It's imperative for the Broncos to remain focused on the task at hand. Build on the win over Kansas City with the goal of playing a complete game. — Ian St. Clair Score more points than Carolina My advanced analytics came through once again. For the 6th time this season, the Broncos have scored more points than their opponent and won. Following this trend, if they do that this Sunday against the Panthers, they will improve to 7-2. — Scotty Payne Scotty's analytics are spot on. One of the best ways to ensure his analytics remain proven correct is to limit the Panthers' ability to run the football. That forces Carolina into a one-dimensional attack and allows the defensive line to eventually pin its ears back and make Bryce Young as uncomfortable as the back of a Volkswagen. — Adam Malnati Keep feeding Jonah Coleman Good things happen when you run the ball effectively. We saw that for the Broncos in their past two victories. Last Sunday, rookie running back Jonah Coleman was solid on the ground for the Denver. He certainly deserves the majority of carries moving forward. The Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the league and give up nearly 5 yards per carry. Why not pound the ball on the ground and keep giving Coleman a chance to prove himself even more? away.blurb: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II not assigned game status, 4 Broncos listed as questionable for Week 8 game vs. Chiefs Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Cornerback Pat Surtain II appears poised to return to the field for the Broncos. Surtain (ankle) was a full participant for the third consecutive practice, and he was not assigned a game status for Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs. The absence of a game status indicates Surtain will be available to play. While Surtain is expected to make his return, four Broncos are listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game. Defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring), tackle Garett Bolles (hip), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) are questionable for the division matchup. All four players were limited in Friday's practice. Running back RJ Harvey (knee) — who was added the Broncos' injury report on Thursday — and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both ruled out. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health. CBS has the broadcast, and the Texans are favored by 4.5 points, with the total sitting at 40.5. That’s a pretty low number, but take one look at the Chargers’ offense and you’ll understand it. Los Angeles still hasn’t won a game, and Houston hasn’t exactly been lighting up the scoreboard, either. This might not be the prettiest game on Sunday’s schedule. Check out our free NFL picks for more predictions. Houston Texans Need to Take Advantage of This Matchup Houston is 2-5 and coming off its bye week. The Texans lost 27-21 to the Giants in overtime before the break, which was a pretty disappointing result considering they were favored by 10 points. Houston had finally started to turn things around with consecutive victories, then went right back to making mistakes against a team it should have beaten. That’s what bothers me about the Texans. They’ve got enough talent to be better than 2-5, but they haven’t been consistent enough to trust. The offense can move the ball, but finishing drives has been a problem. Against the Chargers, Houston doesn’t need to get into a scoring contest. It needs to avoid turnovers, establish the run, and make Los Angeles prove it can score. The extra week of preparation should help. Houston has had time to work on some of the problems that showed up against New York, and now it gets a Chargers team that’s struggling badly. But I’d still like to see the Texans put together a complete game before giving them too much credit. They’ve been favored before and found ways to lose. Los Angeles Chargers Are Running Out of Answers The Chargers are 0-7 after losing 24-9 to the Rams on Sunday. Nine points, all on field goals. That’s a pretty rough afternoon, especially when you’re playing in your own stadium. Los Angeles was only down 10-9 at halftime, so the game was there for the taking. Then the Chargers went scoreless in the second half. And that’s the problem with this team. The defense can keep things respectable for a while, but the offense hasn’t been doing enough to win. Los Angeles also lost 22-6 to Kansas City in Week 6. That’s 15 points over those two games, and you’re not beating many NFL teams with that kind of production. I will say this for the Chargers. They’re at home, and Houston hasn’t been particularly impressive. If Los Angeles can get its running game going and avoid putting everything on the passing attack, it might be able to hang around. But the Chargers have to start finishing drives. Settling for field goals is one thing. Going an entire half without scoring is another. Houston Texans vs Los Angeles Chargers Picks and Prediction Spread Pick: Houston Texans -4.5 I’m laying the 4.5 with Houston. I know the Texans are 2-5, and that’s not exactly the kind of record that makes you want to rush to the betting window. But the Chargers are winless, and their offense has been miserable. Los Angeles scored nine points against the Rams and six against Kansas City. Houston doesn’t need to be spectacular to cover this number. It just needs to get into the low 20s and make the Chargers chase the game. The bye week helps, too. Give me the Texans to win by at least a touchdown. Total Pick: Under 40.5 Give me the under 40.5. Normally, I’d be a little nervous taking an under this low, but I keep coming back to the Chargers’ offense. Fifteen points over their last two games against the Rams and Chiefs isn’t much to work with. Houston has also had trouble finishing drives, so I don’t expect the Texans to put up 35. This looks like a game where both teams spend plenty of time trying to establish the run and avoid mistakes. The danger is a defensive touchdown or a couple of short fields. Otherwise, I can see something like 23-13, and that stays under. away.blurb: DeMeco Ryans: “Getting Jalen back, it'll be very beneficial for us, just how versatile of a player he is, how smart he is, how fast and physical he plays. He really raises the physical nature of our defense when he's out there. I was excited to get him back in action today.” Ryans: “Our team came out today ready to work. They showed that on Monday when we went out to practice. There has been really great intent, very deliberate practice from everybody. I really love the energy, love the execution, love how guys are operating. I'm excited to see how we continue to progress this week and keep the great practices going. One day is, ‘Okay, can we do it consecutive days? Can all of that translate to Sunday?’” Ryans: “As I look at the Chargers, their team is definitely not indicative of their record. They are a really good football team. Their quarterback is a really great player. Their defense has been really good. Their defense is styled on third down. They eliminate the explosives. This is a really good team. We don't come in looking at the record and making any predetermined notions of who this team is. We go out, we watch the film, we prepare for a really good team. They're a very intricate offense. They move guys around a lot, have a lot of things that can get your eyes if you're not careful. Mike [McDaniel] does a really good job of scheming that in the run. I think they'll stick to the run. We have to do a great job of defending the run. Some issues that we had in the previous week of not defending the run well there late in the football game. It's the same thing this week. We've got to defend it for four quarters. If we do that, we feel that'll be one of the keys to this game. We also understand [Justin] Herbert and his abilities to make plays, especially him in the pocket. We haven't seen a quarterback who is tough as he is in a pocket to be able to shake defenders off and still complete the ball downfield. We have to do a great job of rushing together as a unit with our four guys. We have to do a great job of coverage as well.” Ryans: “We'll see more of Tank. That’s not because of who's out. It's Tank's second week now playing. I think his reps will just increase with his workload. He's put a lot of work in on the side and just natural progression of an increase in his workload.” Ryans: “David is still sidelined. He'll be out. We're still trying to get him on the field, trying to get him going. But right now, it's still week to week. He has made some progress.” Ryans: “Defensively, we have to play together. A concussion absence typically lasts around one to three weeks for most players around the league, but with Blankenship's newly discovered hand surgery, there's a chance that it takes more time for him to return as a starter on the back end of the Texans' defense. For any time that Blankenship is set to remain out for the Texans' secondary, the name to keep an eye on will be veteran MJ Stewart, who returned from his lengthy absence due to a quad injury earlier this year, and was elevated to a starter last week against the Giants as a plug-and-play replacement. Texans safety Reed Blankenship, who remains in concussion protocol, also had surgery on his left hand not long after the Jaguars game, per a source. The Texans will see how he progress through the week. It's effectively the end of what's been a productive second season for Noel. The wideout stepped into an increasingly significant role on the offensive side as an explosive, big-play threat and weapon for C.J. Stroud, ending as Houston's leading receiver in terms of total yards after eight weeks. Through the seven games that Noel played, he had put together 19 receptions for 331 yards and two touchdowns. His 17.4 yards per reception and 14.4 yards per target also lead the entire NFL, which gives some good perspective on just how much of a playmaker the second-year wideout was in a small sample size. And now that the Texans are officially back from the bye week and headed into Week 9, we've now gotten a chance to hear from head coach DeMeco Ryans about Noel's injury. What DeMeco Ryans Said About Jaylin Noel's Injury On Monday, Ryans spoke about what the injury to Noel means for the Texans' offense and special teams unit, noting that his explosiveness and production will be missed, but his absence will also open the door for others around the roster to step up in his place. "So, we'll miss that production from him. And with that being said, a lot of times, you miss a guy, that's someone else's opportunity to step up and fill that void." "We still have five good receivers that we that we like on our roster. We feel like they can still all provide some explosive plays for us. away.headline: Texans lose WR Jaylin Noel to season-ending toe injury
away.blurb: According to multiple reports, the Houston Texans are placing Noel on the season-ending injured reserve after suffering a turf toe injury in Week 7's loss to the New York Giants . Houston's top big-play threat will not return for the rest of the regular season and perhaps the postseason, though sitting with a mere two wins doesn't seem promising for a playoff bid entering November. Noel also served as the team's primary return man on both kickoffs and punts, averaging over 11.0 yards per punt return. Now, Houston has weapons. Earlier this month, the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals in exchange for a second-round pick. Last week against the Giants, Tank Dell return for the first time in nearly two years. Texans lose WR Jaylin Noel to season-ending toe injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Texans lose WR Jaylin Noel to season-ending toe injury Cole Thompson, Texans Wire · Texans Wire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:57 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jaylin Noel's breakout second season has officially come to an end. Based on his timeline in Sunday's matchup, Noel suffered the injury with roughly nine minutes left in regulation after returning a kickoff from the Giants. Based on the report, he appeared to have twisted his toe on the turf and was seen leaving the stadium in a boot. In a corresponding move, the Texans claimed former Cowboys and Cardinals running back Emari Demercado off waivers after his release on Tuesday. He'll join the active roster once the team returns from the bye week. Not only is this a big blow for Noel's promising sophomore season, but it's a loss for the passing game in general. The former Iowa State was led the team with 331 receiving yards to go along with catches and two receiving touchdowns. Noel is the second Texans receiver and the second Iowa State pass-catcher to suffer a season-ending injury this year, joing second-round pick Jayden Higgins, who suffered a torn ACL in August. Dell had one catch for 43 yards on just 10 snaps. Harrison caught a touchdown pass on the same drive and only played in 14 snaps. Both will have a larger role when the team returns from the bye week to take on the Los Angeles Chargers. Things aren’t getting any better soon on that front, as the Chargers may put Derwin James on the IR with a hamstring injury. Outside of Biadasz, only seven players could return for the season. Rashawn Slater's absence is the most detrimental. The Chargers' offensive line entered the season with some major question marks, and that unit remains among the most worrisome. picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he's posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots' chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic's playoff simulator . Green Bay's path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. If Green Bay can split their trip to New England and their Week 10 game against the Minnesota Vikings, who are sitting in the driver's seat in the NFC North at the moment, they have about a 50-50 chance of making the playoffs going into their Week 11 bye week. picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. up with one of the best matchups of the Sunday schedule. Green Bay is 4-1 in the last five, and Jordan Love is playing like an MVP candidate with 10 touchdowns and four interceptions in that five-game span, whereas Drake Maye and the Patriots are 4-1 in the same span with 14 touchdowns to two picks. New England’s defense will be put to the test this week after facing the Dolphins on the road last week (24-19). New England’s defense ranks ninth in points per game allowed (20.3) and 11th in third-down defense (38.5%). The Patriots’ last three wins have come over the Dolphins, Jets, and Raiders, and they only have two wins against teams with a winning record (BUF, PIT). This game smells like one that could come down to the final possession. One area New England has struggled in is the turnover margin. New England is a -0.9 team turnover margin per game, ranking tied for second-worst with the Chargers, ahead of only the Colts (-1.4). Maye did not throw a pick last week in Miami, but New England fumbled three times and three more at home versus the Jets a few weeks ago. Green Bay’s defense looks like it’s found something with J onathan Gannon lately. The Packers have held their last five opponents to 20 or fewer points per game and allowed 14.6 points per game in that span. Green Bay’s offense has been reliant on Jordan Love more than ever. He’s thrown the ball 40-plus times in three straight games and five out of eight on the year. The running game is starting to come around with Josh Jacobs back, but Jacobs hasn’t alleviated the pressure from Love yet. Jacobs had 36 and 39 rushing yards on 11 and 21 carries. He played on a short week, but was impactful in the pass game with 11 catches on 13 targets for 68 yards and two touchdowns. Jacobs already has three scores, so he’s making the biggest impact in the red zone. New England allows 3.0 red zone trips per game (11th) and a 54.1% touchdown-allowed rate in the red zone (12th), compared to Carolina and Detroit, who both rank in the bottom five in those categories. We could see both offenses stall out in the red zone. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable
away.blurb: Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Packers make late add to injury report, list CB Keisean Nixon as questionable The Green Bay Packers added cornerback Keisean Nixon to the injury report before Thursday night's showdown with the Carolina Panthers . The team says Nixon is questionable to play with a shoulder injury. Nixon joins four other questionable players for the Packers: receiver Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder), defensive linemen Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quad). Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and right guard Travis Glover (knee) have all been ruled out for Thursday night. Not having Nixon available on Thursday night would push either Carrington Valentine or Benjamin St-Juste into the starting lineup opposite rookie Brandon Cisse. St-Juste is expected to return after missing two games with a hamstring injury. Kamal Hadden is also available at corner. He has not missed a game since joining the Packers before the 2022 season, appearing in all 75 regular season games. Nixon started the first seven games of the 2026 season as the defense's left cornerback. The Packers defense is about to face ascending young receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards entering Week 8. Gameday inactives are due for the Packers and Panthers at around 5:45 p.m. CT.

away.headline: Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Injury update for Packers WR
away.blurb: The 23-year-old had originally been listed as "questionable" due to shoulder and foot injuries, but he was able to suit up for his eighth game of the season. Golden logged a "limited" practice session on Wednesday after being listed as a non-participant in both Monday's estimated injury report and Tuesday's actual practice session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Golden would be available Thursday during a news conference on Tuesday, Oct. 27. LaFleur also pointed out that the nature of the short week would lead to most sessions being a walkthrough, so his players wouldn't get "any real reps" in advance of the game. The Green Bay Packers are preparing to take on the Carolina Panthers on " Thursday Night Football " in Week 8, marking the second time they have played an NFC South team on a short week this season. This time around, there are questions about whether the Packers will have one of their top wide receivers, Matthew Golden , at their disposal for the game. Golden is dealing with shoulder and foot injuries that have cast doubt on his availability for Thursday's game against the Packers. Golden has appeared in all seven Packers games so far in 2026. He has enjoyed a breakout season, tallying 36 catches for 540 yards and three touchdowns, though he has committed a league-high six drops. Here's what to know about Golden's status for the Packers' Week 8 game against the Panthers and how Green Bay may replace him if he cannot play. Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Golden is officially active for the Packers' Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Panthers. Golden playing isn't a major surprise. NFL Media's Ian Rapoport provided a positive update on the second-year receiver during a Thursday, Oct. 29, appearance on "Good Morning Football." "I'm told he's trending towards playing," Rapoport said . "So, there's a good chance for the Packers that Matthew Golden does get on the field today." "I sure hope so," LaFleur responded . "But again, we're still kind of working through it." "We will have a short indie tomorrow, but to move guys around to see how they look," LaFleur said, describing the team's practice procedures. "But certainly hopeful for [Golden]." Who is Matthew Golden's backup? J. Michael Sturdivant is listed as Golden's primary backup on the Packers' official depth chart . The undrafted rookie from Florida has played sparingly through six games, notching three catches for 22 yards, all of which came in Green Bay's Week 3 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. But while Sturdivant is listed as Golden's backup, Savion Williams and Bo Melton have each logged more snaps than the Florida product. As such, those two may be more likely to fill in for Golden across from Christian Watson if the former Texas star can't play. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. home.headline: San Francisco 49ers coach shuts down reunion talks as Brandon Aiyuk seeks NFL reinstatement
home.blurb: Aiyuk filed for NFL reinstatement this week alongside new agent Drew Rosenhaus and is scheduled to report Friday, though the 49ers do not plan to retain him. While general manager John Lynch previously struck a softer tone regarding a potential return for the expensive wideout, Shanahan’s position has remained firm. Beyond mocking Shanahan’s demeanor and leadership, Aiyuk drew severe backlash for taking thinly veiled jabs at Shanahan’s car accident in July , posting Instagram stories telling him to "stay in yo own lane" and declaring that "you can't win the race if you crash out." Brandon Aiyuk won't be getting a warm welcome back in San Francisco after walking away from the team and embarking on an erratic, self-destructive stretch that has effectively alienated him from the NFL. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan officially slammed the door on a reunion Wednesday. Despite San Francisco’s depleted receiver room, the organization has no intention of bringing Aiyuk back, even after the former All-Pro claimed he is cleaning up his act. When asked Wednesday about Aiyuk's apparent turnaround, Shanahan was blunt. "None. I have no expectation," Shanahan said. "I’ve kind of moved on with that mentally and doing kind of how I talked to you guys two months ago. Nothing’s really changed for me." Aiyuk spent months burning bridges across the organization. He severed ties with the franchise through an acrimonious contract standoff, an off-field reckless speeding citation and completely ghosting team medical staff during injury rehabilitation. After San Francisco voided his future contract guarantees and sidelined him, Aiyuk went scorched-earth on social media . He blasted the organization as "stupid," accused Lynch of showing up uninvited at his home and hurled insults at front-office personnel and assistant coaches. Before the fallout, Aiyuk stood as one of San Francisco’s most dynamic offensive playmakers. Selected 25th overall in the 2020 NFL Draft, he developed into the team’s primary perimeter target, posting consecutive 1,000-yard receiving campaigns in 2022 and 2023. His peak came in 2023, when he earned Second-Team All-Pro honors after amassing 1,342 receiving yards and playing a pivotal role in San Francisco’s run to Super Bowl LVIII. Across five seasons in the Bay Area, Aiyuk totaled 294 receptions for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns. Under contract through 2028 with $27 million in guarantees already voided, releasing Aiyuk leaves San Francisco with a $12.35 million dead-cap hit, finally clearing the path for him to pursue opportunities elsewhere. However, despite the news of Aiyuk's push to make an NFL return, with plans to return to the 49ers facility on Friday, the 49ers are likely to cut him before then. Why? Well, the team has made clear they have no plans to keep Aiyuk around. home.headline: AWOL NFL star files for bombshell return to 49ers roster... despite active arrest warrant
home.blurb: Even if he is reinstated, however, Aiyuk is unlikely to ever return to the field for the 49ers. According to ESPN, the most likely outcome is San Francisco releasing him. Shanahan was asked Wednesday what his response was to news of Aiyuk's planned return. 'None,' he said. 'I have no expectation. I've kind of moved on with that mentally... nothing has really changed for me.' 'You can't win the race if you crash out,' Aiyuk said about Shanahan, who suffered a broken hand, three broken ribs and a concussion in a crash that nearly cost him his eye. MORE: NFL bad boy Dre Greenlaw handed huge fine for sucker-punching rival Exiled NFL star Brandon Aiyuk has filed paperwork to be reinstated, with the 49ers wide receiver reportedly expected back at the practice facility on Friday. That is despite Aiyuk being the subject of an active arrest warrant in Santa Clara County - where the 49ers' facility is situated - after he was allegedly caught driving at 104mph outside Levi's Stadium earlier this year. Aiyuk has not played an NFL game since tearing knee ligaments in October 2024, with many fearing for his future after a chaotic offseason saw him fail to report for training camp and threaten to tank his career to force an exit from San Francisco. He is on the 49ers' reserve/did not report list but Aiyuk's new agent said Wednesday that the wide receiver is now plotting a comeback. 'Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,' Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN . Both general manager John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan have suggested the wide receiver will not play another game for the 49ers. While the receiver is on the reserve/did not report list, the 49ers do not have to pay Aiyuk or make a spot for him on their roster. San Francisco previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 after he failed to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer while rehabilitating his knee injury. In fact, Aiyuk has collected only $48.1 million of his four-year, $120 million contract extension. He was due a $24.9 million option bonus on September 1. The 28-year-old has faced significant criticism over his antics and posts on social media in recent months, including crude jokes he made about Shanahan's offseason car crash. Aiyuk had fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until Rosenhaus said on Monday that he had been hired. The receiver has previously suggested he wants to play alongside his former college teammate Jayden Daniels on the Washington Commanders.

home.headline: Brandon Aiyuk Applies for NFL Reinstatement, Will Report to 49ers Facility, Agent Says
home.blurb: Brandon Aiyuk has taken another step in his attempt to return to the NFL by applying for reinstatement after being placed on the reserve/left squad list by the San Francisco 49ers in December 2025. While there isn’t much positivity about the Seattle Seahawks from fans following the team’s blowout loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday, that hasn’t slowed confidence from oddsmakers ahead of their Week 9 game. According to the current odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks enter their second game against the Arizona Cardinals as 10.5-point favorites (-110) , with Seattle’s moneyline is set at -650 , while Arizona’s sits at +480 . The over/under line for the game is 44.5 , indicating that the Seahawks, now 4-4, are more than likely headed for another defensive slogfest against the Cardinals. The man trusted to score those points for the Cardinals will be none other than Washington State alum Gardner Minshew, who brought his patented good vibes to Arizona in the team’s second-half upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Minshew ignited a spark in the Cardinals’ offense, which helped them score the most points, 33, that they’ve scored in a game all year. Arizona’s gutsy win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys lifted them to 3-5 on the season. Aside from Minshew, running back Tyler Allgier had a career day after taking over for rookie Jeremiyah Love. The journeyman quarterback’s favorite target was Michael Wilson, who willed his team to a win with two broken ribs. The health of Wilson may be paramount to the Cardinals’ offense as he offers a second option for Minshew when superstar tight end Trey McBride is covered. While the Cardinals beat up on a reeling Cowboys’ defense, a trip to Seattle to play Mike Macdonald’s unit is an entirely different story. This unit held the Cardinals to 7 points in Week 2 and stifled much of Arizona’s run game. However, the story of these two teams’ early meeting was the Seahawks’ offense, which totaled 24 points in the second half after a slow start. Seattle, which was led by Drew Lock at the time, was led by their offensive engine, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN totaled three touchdowns and 155 yards in that game, a performance the struggling Seahawks would love to see again. Unlike most of their games in 2026, the Seahawks had success on the ground in Week 2 with Emmanuel Wilson running for 92 yards and rookie Jadarian Price adding 52 yards. With Zach Charbonnet back, this matchup looks on paper to be the perfect bounce-back after they struggled to do much of anything on the ground against Chicago. With the pressure turned up on the .500 Seahawks, the oddsmakers appear to predict they’ll storm back with a win over their underdog story division rivals. Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8.
