Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. away.headline: Buccaneers' Yaya Diaby suffers Grade 2 MCL sprain
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain and is expected to miss time, although a return within a matter of weeks is possible. Head coach Todd Bowles confirmed Monday that Diaby sprained his MCL and said he hopes he will avoid injured reserve. Diaby exited in the first quarter and did not return to the Week 8 contest. The official NFL gamebook shows he played just seven of Tampa Bay's 53 defensive snaps (13%), forcing the Buccaneers to adjust their edge rotation. The injury interrupts Diaby's momentum after he recorded three sacks for 21 lost yards against Carolina in Week 7. Tampa Bay managed to shut out Atlanta without recording a sack, relying instead on four interceptions from Michael Penix Jr. No official return date has been announced. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost edge rusher Yaya Diaby to a knee injury during Sunday's 16-0 shutout of the Atlanta Falcons, and the latest reports indicate he could miss multiple games. Rookie Rueben Bain Jr. led the group with 35 snaps (66%), followed by David Walker with 25 (47%), Al-Quadin Muhammad with 23 (43%), and Anthony Nelson with 16 (30%). Diaby's potential absence creates an opportunity for Walker, who leads Tampa Bay with four sacks, and Bain to take on additional responsibilities. The Buccaneers face Chicago in Week 9 before their bye, giving them an extra week to recover before their next game. away.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
away.blurb: Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team’s previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers’ Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team’s final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday’s contest. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers began preparations for their Week 9 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Wednesday, releasing their first injury report ahead of Sunday night’s game at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay listed eight players on the initial report, including three who did not participate in practice. The Buccaneers are coming off a 16-0 shutout victory over Atlanta, their second consecutive win, and will look to continue that momentum against a Chicago team that enters the matchup at 6-2 following a Monday night victory over Seattle. The Buccaneers and Bears are scheduled to kick off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. One NFL insider believes the Vikings could be planning to "soft" bench Murray for this weekend's game, using his lingering injury as an excuse to turn to veteran Carson Wentz. "We're going to actively pursue every avenue we can to make that happen," Phillips said. While Phillips didn't point to any specific changes, NFL analyst Mike Florio suggested that the team could be using Murray's lingering hamstring tightness as an excuse to make a change at quarterback. "It's hard not to look at the current status of Murray's hamstring "tightness" as cover for a soft benching of Murray," Florio wrote . Florio added that Wentz has the best track record of success with top wide receiver Justin Jefferson . "We can't underestimate this Justin Jefferson wrinkle," Florio added. "Of all the quarterbacks they've had the past few years since Kirk Cousins, the one who has the best and most consistent connection with Justin Jefferson is Carson Wentz." Bills Made Changes on Defense The Vikings will face a Bills team that made some significant changes on defense. The team announced this week that they were releasing safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who struggled in coverage and was coming off a one-game suspension for spitting on a Las Vegas Raiders player. The Bills could instead turn to veteran safety Geno Stone , who was elevated from the practice squad for last week's win over the Baltimore Ravens . Stone played in 19 snaps on defense, making six tackles with one pass defensed, while also playing on special teams. Some insiders believe the Bills will seek more help before the NFL trade deadline, though any additions likely wouldn't be ready to contribute for Monday's game against the Vikings. The Bills could instead look to Tre'Davious White for help, with a potential practice squad elevation for the veteran cornerback who returned to the team in late October. picks.blurb: Two 6-1 teams, one marquee matchup. The Bills visit Minnesota after beating the Ravens 36-10, while the Vikings look to rebound from their first loss, a 19-15 defeat in Detroit. Kyler Murray's hamstring is the biggest injury to watch. Kevin O'Connell said Murray remained under evaluation Monday. Carson Wentz is the next option if Murray cannot play but, even if he starts, his mobility deserves attention. Wentz guided the Vikings to wins over the Packers and Bears in September, completing 59% of his passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Minnesota's protection is another concern. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is dealing with shoulder soreness. His availability becomes especially important if Murray's hamstring limits his ability to escape pressure. Josh Allen's supporting cast needs monitoring, too. Joshua Palmer injured his hamstring against Baltimore, DJ Moore picked up another injury concern, and right tackle Spencer Brown missed that game with a back issue. Their practice participation will matter this week. The early market favors Buffalo on the road. The Bills are favorites of -3/-3.5 points, depending on where you do your shopping, and the total has dropped from 48.5 at open to as low as 45.5. Murray's status could move both numbers. If you're curious to read a couple of interesting trends: The Vikings are a perfect 7-0 SU and ATS in the fourth quarter this season, while the Bills are 6-0-1 SU and 7-0 ATS in the second quarter. These are shocking stats when you consider the teams are a combined 12-2 on the year, but just thought we'd pass it along. Vikings vs Bills odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Bills -3.5 Moneyline: Bills -170; Vikings +155 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Vikings vs Bills USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bills 24, Vikings 20 Do we have a Super Bowl preview on our hands? Guess that depends how you feel about Minnesota's offense and Buffalo's defense. Either way, we've got a pair of 6-1 teams, a few superstar talents in Josh Allen, James Cook and Justin Jefferson, plus a banged up Kyler Murray with a hamstring injury that could move the line before kickoff. Whether it's Murray or Carson Wentz stepping in for him again, I still trust the Bills more to manufacture points. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense will make Allen work for everything – as the Lions just experienced in their low-scoring win – but the visitors simply have more at their disposal and I like them to remain unbeaten on the road. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bills 21, Vikings 14 For a team that was the league's last undefeated group standing, the Vikings are facing quite a bit of strife. A rickety offense might soon become fully broken if Kyler Murray continues to miss on downfield opportunities. Jim Leonhard's defense has hardly been a bunch of world-beaters, but the opportunistic group continues to come up with big plays in key moments, particularly with its pass rush. If the Bills can get Murray off schedule, it could be a difficult evening for Minnesota. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Vikings 21, Bills 16 Offense or defense? Like Week 8, the Vikings find themselves in a matchup that features strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness. It was the Lions offense that triumphed against the Vikings defense, but there's reason to believe things could be different this week. Buffalo has been much looser with the football this year, turning it over 11 times – which ranks 11th-most in the league, while Detroit has the third-fewest. Suddenly, you see the Vikings' path to victory. Brian Flores' defense forces Josh Allen into a mistake or two on Monday night and that is the difference. home.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR.
